avoid anything that could be stressful

issues.item: Never Alone: make sure never to be alone with another person
issues.explanation: 'Never Alone' is hard to reconcile with the trauma type of police violence and the rest of the profile. This item more strongly suggests fear of being alone with a potentially abusive intimate or familiar person, whereas the threat items center on strangers and general vigilance. That mismatch is difficult to explain clinically within the same trauma-linked profile.

issues.item: Contamination: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened
issues.explanation: 'Contamination' is not well aligned with the trauma type and accompanying appraisals. Feeling dirty or contaminated is more characteristic of sexual trauma; with police violence, and with the current memory/threat content, this appraisal stands out as clinically incongruent rather than merely unusual.

vignette: Dr. Samuel has been a dentist for over three decades, but his career and life took a sharp turn after an incident of police violence that he experienced two years ago. During a routine traffic stop, Samuel was unjustly targeted and subjected to excessive force by the police, leaving him with both physical scars and deep psychological wounds. Samuel had come to believe that there was something inherently flawed about himself that made the event happen—a belief that intensified whenever he recalled the traumatic incident. These memories often felt alienated from his own experience; they seemed like they belonged to someone else rather than to him, yet the auditory recall and physical pain he experienced during these flashbacks were vivid reminders of the trauma. The memory of what happened continues to haunt Samuel’s daily life. He would often hear the loud commands from that night ringing in his head as if it were happening again, and the physical pain in his shoulder where he was struck seemed almost real. These memories triggered a relentless cycle of maladaptive strategies: he started avoiding anything that could cause negative or positive feelings, believing that any strong emotion might bring back unwanted memories. He also avoided stressful situations entirely, leading him to miss important dental conferences and social gatherings. Samuel’s intense fear of strangers approaching him in ordinary situations was another critical component of his post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The constant threat he perceived from the outside world made it difficult for him to feel safe, even within his own home or office. This perception of threat only deepened his negative appraisals; he felt that his life had been irrevocably destroyed by the trauma and that the injustice of what happened to him was never properly addressed. To cope with this constant sense of danger, Samuel developed a habit of checking his surroundings for any signs of potential threats. He constantly scanned his environment, looking for anything suspicious or unfamiliar. This hyper-vigilance extended even to choosing where he sat in social settings based on how safe and protected he felt. The more he engaged in these maladaptive strategies, the more intense his memories became, leading him to avoid more situations that could potentially trigger them. Samuel’s occupation as a dentist has been significantly impacted by his PTSD symptoms. He started avoiding patients who reminded him of his trauma or those with whom he had any interaction that caused stress. His avoidance of feelings and stressful situations led him to cancel appointments and eventually, even consider retiring from his profession, which he once loved. The relentless cycle of negative appraisals, memories, threat perceptions, and maladaptive strategies has progressively tightened its grip on Samuel’s life over the past two years. He is now seeking help because he recognizes that his current state is unsustainable, both personally and professionally. What frightens him most is the fear that he will never fully recover from this traumatic event and that he may lose more of what he holds dear in his life. Despite these fears, Samuel also hopes for a way to regain control over his life and find peace with his past experiences. He hopes therapy can provide him with the tools to manage his symptoms and ultimately lead a fulfilling life once again.
